title: Closed components, reduced unions and intersections at ordinary stalks
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth, def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and $H\hookrightarrow X$ a closed subscheme [def-weil-closed-immersion] with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf]. For a point $x\in X$ and an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ containing $x$, let $\mathfrak p$ correspond to $x$ and let $I\subseteq B$ define $H\cap U$. The stalk ideal $\mathcal I_x$ is $IB_{\mathfrak p}$, and if $x\in H$ then $\mathcal O_{H,x}=B_{\mathfrak p}/IB_{\mathfrak p}$ via the canonical quotient-localization isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If $x\notin H$, then $\mathcal I_x=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. Finite scheme-theoretic intersections of closed subschemes (the scheme-theoretic intersection of closed subschemes $H_1,\ldots,H_n$ with ideal sheaves $\mathcal I_1,\ldots,\mathcal I_n$ is the closed subscheme cut out by the sum $\mathcal I_1+\cdots+\mathcal I_n$, and for $n=0$ it is $X$) have stalk ideal the sum of their stalk ideals. If $Z_1,\ldots,Z_n$ are reduced closed subschemes, the reduced induced closed subscheme on $|Z_1|\cup\cdots\cup|Z_n|$ has, at every $x\in X$, stalk ideal the intersection of the stalk ideals of the $Z_i$ (reducedness of the $Z_i$ is needed: on $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbb Z[s]$ the single closed subscheme $V(s^2)$ has reduced union ideal $(s)\neq(s^2)$). Suppose now that $H$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Its finitely many irreducible components with reduced induced structure [def-weil-irreducible-components, lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] are distinct integral closed subschemes [def-pc-integral-scheme] whose reduced union equals $H$. For every $x\in X$, taking the stalk ideal gives a bijection from the components containing $x$ to the prime ideals of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ minimal over $\mathcal I_x$. Components not containing $x$ have unit stalk ideal. The stalk ideal of $H$ is the intersection of the ideals of its components through $x$; the empty intersection is the unit ideal. No regularity of $X$ or of the components is assumed.

Tag 0BIA (lemma-strict-normal-crossings), components through a point and coordinate prime ideals; Schemes Tag 01J3 (lemma-reduced-closed-subscheme), Algebra Tags 00ES and 00E3. Proof handoff retained verbatim under the released re-split order; these are the old parent arguments to implement, not proof steps of this statement-only node. Original parent step 1: We work throughout on affine neighborhoods $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ in $X$, with $B$ Noetherian. If $x$ corresponds to $\mathfrak p$ and a closed subscheme $Z\cap U$ has ideal $J$, its local ring at $x\in Z$ is $B_{\mathfrak p}/JB_{\mathfrak p}$. This follows from the affine description of a closed immersion and localization of a quotient. Finite intersections of closed subschemes have ideal the sum of the ideals: a ring map kills every ideal precisely when it kills their sum. A finite family of reduced closed subschemes with union of supports $T$ has reduced union ideal the intersection of their ideals: on $U$, this intersection is radical and has vanishing set $T\cap U$, so uniqueness of the reduced induced structure applies. Finite intersections of ideals commute with localization: if $a/s$ lies in every localized ideal, choose one denominator outside $\mathfrak p$ for each membership and multiply these finitely many denominators. Thus the same union and intersection rules hold for the stalk ideals.
Cited statements: def-weil-closed-immersion, lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient, lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme.

Original parent step 7: Choose the finitely many irreducible components of the closed subset $|H|$; their finiteness follows because $X$ is Noetherian. Give each its reduced induced closed subscheme structure and call them $C_i$. They are integral because they are nonempty, reduced and irreducible. The reduced induced structure theorem and reducedness of $H$ show that their reduced union is exactly $H$, rather than a thickening with the same support. The empty closed subset gives the empty family.
Cited statements: lem-sc-noetherian-closed-subset-finite-components, lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme, def-pc-integral-scheme.

Original parent step 8: Fix $x\in H$ and its chosen parameters. The components of $H$ through $x$ correspond exactly to the minimal prime ideals over $(T)$ in $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. To check this using the cited statements, take an affine neighborhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$. Intersecting global irreducible components with $U$ gives the components of $H\cap U$: closure extends an irreducible subset of the open to an irreducible closed subset, and a nonempty open of an irreducible component is dense in it. Apply the spectrum/minimal-prime theorem to its affine ring $B/J$. Then apply the inclusion-preserving prime-localization bijection and the quotient-localization isomorphism. Minimality is preserved for primes below $\mathfrak p$, since every smaller prime is still below $\mathfrak p$. Finally a prime containing $T$ contains some $t_i$; the ideals $(t_i)$ are distinct incomparable primes, by steps 4 and 5. They are therefore exactly the minimal primes over $(T)$. In particular each $C_i$ through $x$ has stalk ideal one distinct $(t_j)$. Components missing $x$ have unit ideal stalk.
Cited statements: lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes, lem-weil-pbc-primes-of-localization, lem-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime-of-quotient, lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme, lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-ideal-stalk-range.

The affine-open stalk localization instance and IsLocalization.algEquiv identify the ambient stalk with B_p, carrying every section germ to b/1. Mapping the ideal through this equivalence gives exactly the extended ideal.

proof.text: By the definition of scheme-theoretic intersection (Stacks Tag 0C4H, definition-scheme-theoretic-intersection-union), its defining ideal is the sum of the defining ideals. On $U$, for ideals $I_1,\ldots,I_n$, localization gives $(\sum_i I_i)B_{\mathfrak p}=\sum_i I_iB_{\mathfrak p}$: each summand on the right is generated by images of elements of $I_i$, which are exactly the generators on the left. Here $(\sum_i\widetilde{I_i})|_U=\widetilde{\sum_iI_i}$, since the sum sheaf is the image of $\bigoplus_i\widetilde{I_i}\to\mathcal O_U$ and $\widetilde{(\ )}$ preserves direct sums and images; so the intersection is cut out on $U$ by $\sum_iI_i$. Apply step 1 to the intersection and to the individual closed subschemes. The empty scheme-theoretic intersection is $X$, whose ideal is the empty sum $0$.

Finite intersections of ideals commute with localization by Mathlib IsLocalization.map_inf, packaged as mapFrameHom. Its preservation of finite infima includes the empty infimum, since the unit ideal maps to the unit ideal. On a fixed affine neighborhood, IdealSheafData.ideal_iInf identifies the ideal of the finite infimum with the finite infimum of the affine ideals. Step 1 and preservation of finite infima give the equality of stalk ideals.

proof.text: Let $T=\bigcup_i|Z_i|$ for the finite family of reduced closed subschemes, and let $T_{\mathrm{red}}$ be its reduced induced structure. Write $J_i$ and $J_T$ for their ideals on $U$. The reduced induced closed-subscheme theorem identifies $J_T$ with the functions vanishing in residue fields at all points of $T\cap U$. The uniqueness clause identifies each $J_i$ with the analogous functions vanishing on $|Z_i|\cap U$, since $Z_i$ is reduced. Vanishing on the union means vanishing on every member, so $J_T=\bigcap_iJ_i$. By steps 1 and 5, $(\mathcal I_T)_x=\bigcap_i(\mathcal I_{Z_i})_x$. For the empty union the vanishing condition is vacuous, giving the unit ideal. The stipulated reducedness is essential: in $\mathbb Z[s]$ the ideals $(s^2)$ and $(s)$ have the same support but only the latter defines its reduced induced structure.

Now assume $H$ reduced. Apply the finite-component theorem to the closed subset $|H|\subseteq X$, obtaining its finitely many distinct irreducible components $C_i$. Each is closed in $X$ since $|H|$ is closed. Give $C_i$ its reduced induced structure using the reduced induced closed-subscheme theorem. Each $C_i$ is nonempty and irreducible by the definition of an irreducible component and is reduced by construction; hence it is integral by the integral-scheme characterization. Their supports cover $|H|$. These are all the irreducible components of $|H|$: a component $C$ is irreducible and covered by the finitely many closed sets $C\cap C_i$, so by the definition of irreducibility $C\subseteq C_i$ for some $i$, and maximality of $C$ gives $C=C_i$; distinct $C_i$ have distinct supports, so the integral closed subschemes are distinct. The uniqueness clause for the reduced induced structure shows that their reduced union is $H$, because $H$ is itself reduced with that support. If $H$ is empty there are no components.

An irreducible closed subset C containing x has nonempty irreducible inverse image in an affine neighborhood U=Spec(B), by the open embedding fromSpec. Its affine vanishing ideal q is therefore prime, and q is contained in the prime p of x. If C and D both contain x, an inclusion of their stalk ideals contracts to the same inclusion of their affine prime ideals, since extension and contraction are inverse on primes below p. The reverse inclusion of affine zero loci follows. The intersection D with U is dense in D, by irreducibility and nonemptiness, so taking closures extends the inclusion back to D contained in C.

proof.text: By step 8 and prime localization, every component through x has prime stalk ideal, and an inclusion between two such ideals forces the reverse inclusion between their supports. Maximality of irreducible components of H and injectivity of the closed embedding imply that the components coincide. Thus their prime stalk ideals form an antichain. By step 6 their finite intersection, including unit ideals of components missing x, is the stalk ideal of H. For any prime Q containing this finite intersection, primality and finite-infimum containment give one component ideal P_j contained in Q; this j must contain x because a prime cannot contain the unit ideal. If Q is minimal it equals P_j. Conversely any prime over the intersection contained in P_j contains a P_k, and the antichain forces k=j and equality. This proves exactly the displayed BijOn, including injectivity and the empty-family case.

proof.text: Apply step 6 to the components constructed in step 7. Their finite reduced union is $H$, so $\mathcal I_x$ is the intersection of all their stalk ideals. By step 3, each component missing $x$ contributes the unit ideal, which can be removed from the intersection. This leaves exactly the components through $x$. If $x\notin H$ there are no such components and both sides are the unit ideal. In that case the unit ideal has no prime ideals above it, so step 9 is the bijection between two empty sets as well. Every preceding argument applies to arbitrary Noetherian $X$; none used regularity.
